questions.q: Put the three stages of a computer's environmental impact in the order they happen.
steps: Manufacture: raw materials are mined and the device is built
Use: electricity is consumed for as long as it runs
Disposal: the device becomes electronic waste
questions.feedback: A full answer in the exam covers all three, not just the electricity.

questions.q: Explain why throwing away an old smartphone is an environmental problem.

markPoints.concept: it contains toxic materials such as lead and mercury
markPoints.exemplar: It contains toxic materials such as lead and mercury.

markPoints.concept: which can leak into the ground and water if it goes to landfill
markPoints.exemplar: These can leak into the ground and water if it goes to landfill.

markPoints.concept: and valuable materials are wasted that could have been recovered
markPoints.exemplar: Valuable materials that could have been recycled are wasted.

questions.example: A smartphone contains toxic materials including lead and mercury, and if it goes to landfill those can leach into the soil and into the water supply. It also contains valuable metals such as gold and copper which could have been recovered, so throwing it away wastes them and means more has to be mined.
questions.paraphrase: These devices hold poisonous substances that can contaminate the ground and water once dumped, and they also contain precious metals which are simply lost rather than being reclaimed.
questions.feedback: Three ideas: what is in it, what that does, and what is wasted.

questions.q: Which of these reduce the environmental impact of computing? Tick all that apply.
options: Repairing a device rather than replacing it
Recycling a device at an approved centre
Running data centres on renewable electricity
Buying a new phone every year
correct: Repairing a device rather than replacing it
Recycling a device at an approved centre
Running data centres on renewable electricity
questions.feedback: The greenest device is usually the one somebody already owns.
